title: Polycrisis Resilience in the Global South: Mitigating Human Exposure to Interconnected Global Risks Across the 21st Century and Millennium
subtitle: A Development-Oriented Framework for Reducing Overlapping Climate, Pollution, Poverty, and Conflict Exposure in Developing Economies (2025–3000+)
description: An institutional research monograph applying the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience framework to the Global South. Builds on the 180 billion person-year…
contribution: Establishes the Global South operational architecture for Polycrisis Resilience—targeting 180B person-years of overlapping exposure through nine development multipliers, six resilience dimensions, and three simultaneous intervention levels.
abstract: Developed under Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics, this monograph operationalizes Polycrisis Resilience for the Global South—connecting overlapping exposure environments, nine development multipliers, and cumulative person-years avoided across the 21st century and millennium.

keyFindings.title: The Global South Faces the Acute Core of the Polycrisis: Intersecting climate change, air and water pollution, poverty, demographic expansion, resource insecurity, and conflict concentrate roughly 180 billion person-years of overlapping multi-hazard exposure across 2025–2100.

Development Itself Is Polycrisis Risk Reduction: Progress across nine core interventions—clean energy, clean cooking, digital infrastructure, education, resilient infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, institutions, and water/sanitation—delivers multiplicative resilience dividends.

Demographic Timing Governs Century-Scale Exposure: Investments made in the 2026–2035 window shape the infrastructure and survivability conditions inherited by hundreds of millions of future residents in Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and emerging urban hubs.

Three Intervention Levels Must Operate Simultaneously: Preventing exposure (Level 1), reducing vulnerability (Level 2), and strengthening adaptive capacity (Level 3) compress 180B person-years of overlapping exposure down by over 75% across the century.

Context-Specific Regional Execution Is Essential: Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, Southeast Asia, Latin America, MENA, and SIDS face distinct hazard mixes requiring tailored multi-pillar portfolios rather than uniform templates.
